text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Former President Mauno Koivisto in an extensive newspaper article says the central bank strove for political power under bank governors Karjalainen (1979-83) and Kullberg (1983-92).
- Finnish man died of diphtheria -- first fatal case in many years. Doctors amazed Finland has not been hit by epidemic considering diphtheria figures in nearby Russia. @
- Working group proposes Finnish pension funds could invest about two billion markka yearly in the stock market.
- British music magazine "The Gramophone" has given prestigious award to Lahti City Orchestra for its recording of Sibelius's fifth symphony.
- Finnish animal protection society has donated plastic surgical dummies to Helsinki Veterinary school. @
KAUPPALEHTI
- National Board of Taxation has mistakenly taxed dozens of firms on the basis of erroneous assessments. Entrepreneurs' organisation says mistake has driven some firms to bankruptcy.
- Russian import restrictions slated for next year will cut EU vodka exports to Russia by up to 75 percent -- Finnish vodka exports also to be affected.
DEMARI
- Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen, answering questions in parliament, said responsibility for job creation lies with individual EU member states and not with the Union as a body. @
- Green party wants further talks on government's energy tax plans in order to reach a consensus.
AAMULEHTI
- Chairman of the parliamentary defence committee says parliament has been inadequately informed of NATO plans for an expanded partnership for peace.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Finland opposes EU Commission's plans to reduce fishing by 40 percent over the next six years. For Finland, plan would mean scrapping almost one in two salmon and cod fishing boats. @
- Minister of Trade and Industry Antti Kalliomaki says Finland ready to take part in a pan-Nordic electricity market.
- "Tango princess" Tutta Carpelan hopes to win a local council seat in town of Kaarina in October 20 elections.
--Helsinki Newsroom +358-0-680 50 235
